evidence.note: was: Work out the extra tax you'll actually owe on a bonus or commission payment for the year. See the marginal tax rate applied to your lump sum and your actual take-home bonus.

decisions.proposedLead: Tax on a bonus in Australia is the difference between the annual tax on salary alone and the annual tax on salary plus bonus, worked out on the 2026-27 scale; there is no flat bonus tax. For an employee on $90,000 receiving $10,000, that difference is $3,200, so $6,800 of the bonus is kept [[bonusTaxSplit]]. Employers withhold from bonus payments using ATO Schedule 5, and any over-withholding is refunded at tax time.

evidence.note: was: What FBT is, how the Australian tax system calculates fringe benefits, which benefits are exempt, current FBT rates and thresholds, and how reportable fringe benefits affect your take-home pay and tax

decisions.proposedLead: The FBT year runs from 1 April to 31 March [[FBT.yearStart]], not the 1 July to 30 June income year, and fringe benefits tax is paid by employers, not employees, on non-cash benefits. The rate for the FBT year ending 31 March 2026 is 47% [[FBT.rate]], applied to the taxable value grossed up by 2.0802 (Type 1, GST-creditable) or 1.8868 (Type 2) [[FBT.grossUpType1]]. Returns are due 21 May, or 25 June via a tax agent.

evidence.note: was: Calculate your total final pay when leaving a job. Includes unused annual leave payout with loading, notice period pay, long service leave, and estimated tax on your final payment.

decisions.proposedLead: Termination pay (final pay) in Australia is the sum of outstanding wages, unused annual leave, any notice paid in lieu, long service leave and, if the role is made redundant, redundancy pay. Unused annual leave is paid at (annual salary ÷ 260) × leave days, plus 17.5% leave loading [[COMMON_LEAVE_LOADING]] where the award requires it, taxed at the marginal rate in 2026-27; most awards require payment within 7 days.

evidence.note: was: The Medicare levy is 2% of your taxable income — but not from the first dollar. Below $28,011 you pay nothing, and between $28,011 and $35,013 you pay 10% of the excess instead. Work out your exact le

decisions.proposedLead: A Medicare levy calculation has three bands: no levy at or under $28,011 of taxable income, a shade-in of 10% of the amount over $28,011 up to $35,013, and 2% of the whole income above $35,013 [[MEDICARE_LEVY]]. Families get a higher threshold of $47,238 plus $4,338 per dependent child [[MEDICARE_LEVY.familyThreshold]]. These are the 2025-26 thresholds, the latest the ATO has published.

evidence.note: was: Tax rates for foreign residents working in Australia: no tax-free threshold, no LITO, and different brackets. See a side-by-side comparison with resident rates.

decisions.proposedLead: The non-resident tax rate in Australia is 30% on every dollar of Australian-sourced income up to $135,000, then 37% to $190,000 and 45% above, for 2026-27 [[NON_RESIDENT_TAX_BRACKETS]]. Unlike residents, foreign residents get no $18,200 tax-free threshold [[TAX_FREE_THRESHOLD]] and no 15% bracket, but they are not charged the 2% Medicare levy. The rates were unchanged by the 1 July 2026 resident tax cut.

decisions.proposedLead: The minimum wage for an 18-year-old in Australia with no award is $18.06 an hour from 1 July 2026, or $22.58 an hour as a casual [[FWO_PUBLISHED_JUNIOR_RATES]], which is 68.3% of the $26.44 National Minimum Wage [[NMW.hourly]]. Junior rates apply to workers under 21 [[ADULT_AGE]]; in retail, fast food and hospitality a different percentage applies to that award's own base rate.

evidence.note: was: The National Minimum Wage for each financial year since 2010-11 , the size of every Annual Wage Review increase, and what drove the big years.

decisions.proposedLead: The National Minimum Wage is the pay floor for adults aged 21 and over not covered by an award or agreement, reset each year by the Fair Work Commission's Annual Wage Review. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 an hour, or $1,004.90 for a 38-hour week [[NMW]], a 6.0% rise. The rate has increased every year since 2010-11, when it was $15.00 an hour [[NMW_HISTORY]].

evidence.note: was: Your Notice of Assessment is the ATO's official statement of your tax calculation. Here's how to read each line, understand what the numbers mean, and what to do if something doesn't look right.

decisions.proposedLead: A notice of assessment (NOA) is the document the ATO issues after processing an income tax return, setting out taxable income, the tax on that income, credits for tax already withheld and the resulting refund or amount owing. For the 2025-26 return, most online lodgements are assessed within 2 weeks [[RETURN_2026.onlineRefundTypical]] and paper returns within 50 business days [[RETURN_2026.paperRefundBusinessDays]].
